key_insight: The linear, mean-shear-driven contribution to inner-scaled wall-pressure variance appears Reynolds-number invariant at high friction Reynolds number, so the observed logarithmic growth must come from the nonlinear source.
engineering_relevance: This helps isolate which turbulence mechanisms matter for predicting high-Re wall pressure loads on aircraft, turbomachinery, and other wall-bounded flow systems.
method: Used simultaneous hot-wire velocity and velocity-gradient measurements from an eight-sensor probe.
Compared a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer with a high-Re pipe flow.
Examined inner-scaled factors in the linear pressure-source term across Reynolds number and wall distance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports collapse of the inner-scaled linear-source factors across Reynolds number and an inverse-with-wall-distance decay of the relevant inertial-layer velocity-gradient variance, up to friction Reynolds numbers of O(10^4).
watch_item: The conclusion is based on specific canonical wall-bounded flows and the assumed separation of linear and nonlinear Poisson-source contributions, so broader geometry or very different forcing conditions may need separate validation.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
